https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_behavioral_therapy

Was it effective? Do you think it has helped you in life?

I think it is somewhat effective. It takes effort so it's not easy, but it teaches you to question the thoughts that arise and to be more introspective.

One mindfulness teacher said it well: each thought pattern is a trail in the woods. The more traffic it gets, the wider it becomes and the easier it is to follow. Breaking a new trail is difficult and takes time and traffic, all the while the old trail is still there, so wide and easy to follow.

It's not a quick fix -- these techniques should be taught to kids before they encounter burnout or ostracization or other mental health issues.

Yes, I went through 3 courses of it, 2 while active duty and one after exiting the military through the VA. All three of mine were focused very heavily on PTSD recovery. It's a very effective method, in my opinion, of starting to recover. It helps you get a mindset of awareness and mindfulness over yourself, what's happening around you, how you're reacting to it and if those reactions are actually "right". Once you get into that mindset, that semblance of self awareness you're able to recognize when what you're doing isn't the practical or healthy thing to be doing at that time and in that situation and you begin to gain control, to be able to scale back those reactions or thought processes. CBT, CPT, various in vivo programs (especially prolonged exposure) have given me back a semi "normal" life again. I'm not as angry and on edge, small slights are no longer egregious attacks on my person, a group of people walking together isn't a major threat, and going to the store is not walking through the markets of Baqubah.

Hopefully this is still relevant, but here is my experience with it:

  • If you are unaware of it happening, it works.

  • If you are aware of it happening, it does not work if you resist it.

  • If you are aware of it happening, it does work but it can be very emotionally painful.
